mergedParams.userDescription: Shifting color channels and RGB splits. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: RGB Channel Shifts & Splits - Glitch Effects

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'chromatic-aberration-pulse' that simulates RGB channel separation with a pulsing animation. The effect should split the red, green, and blue channels of any target element (text, image, or video) and offset them slightly in different directions, creating a glitchy chromatic aberration effect. Use CSS filters with drop-shadow to simulate channel separation. The effect should pulse in and out with smooth easing, accepting parameters for: intensity (how far channels separate), pulseSpeed (animation duration), and direction (horizontal, vertical, or radial). Implement as a generic effect using AnimationRange keyframes that animate multiple drop-shadow filters simultaneously.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Properties to animate: filter (multiple drop-shadow values for RGB channels). AnimationRange structure: [{key: 'filter', val: 'drop-shadow(0 0 0 rgba(255,0,0,0.8)) drop-shadow(0 0 0 rgba(0,255,0,0.8)) drop-shadow(0 0 0 rgba(0,0,255,0.8))', prog: 0}, {key: 'filter', val: calculated based on intensity/direction, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'filter', val: original, prog: 1}]. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.pulseSpeed || 2, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: animationRanges, easing: 'ease-in-out'}. Input params: Zod schema with intensity (number, 0-20px), pulseSpeed (number, seconds), direction (enum: 'horizontal'|'vertical'|'radial'), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: [effectData]}.

prompts.prompt: Design an internal waveform effect preset called 'bass-rgb-split' that creates audio-reactive RGB channel splitting synchronized to bass frequencies. When bass hits, the red, green, and blue channels should separate and vibrate independently, creating a dynamic glitch effect. The effect should use translateX and translateY transforms combined with CSS mix-blend-mode and opacity to simulate channel separation. Higher bass intensity creates larger channel offsets. Include parameters for: sensitivity (reaction threshold), maxOffset (maximum pixel separation), blendMode (screen, multiply, overlay), and decaySpeed (how quickly channels return). This should be perfect for music videos and beat-driven content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Waveform (audio-reactive). Waveform configuration: {type: 'translate', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: params.sensitivity || 0.7, threshold: 0.3, maxOffset: params.maxOffset || 15}. Additional effects array combining translateX, translateY, and opacity modulations. Effect data: [{type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'parent', mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, props: waveformConfig}, {type: 'generic', ranges: [{key: 'mixBlendMode', val: params.blendMode || 'screen', prog: 0}]}]. Input params: Zod schema with sensitivity (number, 0-1), maxOffset (number, pixels), blendMode (enum), decaySpeed (number, 0-1), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects', dependencies: {presets: []}}. Return: {effects: effectsArray}.

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'glitch-shift-sequence' that creates a cinematic RGB channel shift effect with random glitch intervals. The effect should simulate digital corruption by randomly offsetting color channels at specific intervals, creating a stuttering, glitchy aesthetic. Use a combination of CSS filters (hue-rotate, saturate, contrast) and transform properties. The effect should have distinct 'glitch moments' with smooth transitions between them. Accept parameters for: glitchFrequency (how often glitches occur), glitchIntensity (severity of channel shifts), colorShift (hue rotation amount), and sequenceDuration. Include subtle noise/grain overlay during glitch moments using CSS filters.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Properties: filter (combining hue-rotate, saturate, contrast, blur), transform (translateX, skewX). AnimationRange with multiple keyframes for glitch sequence: prog values at 0, 0.1, 0.15, 0.3, 0.35, 0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.8, 0.85, 1 to create stuttering effect. Filter values alternate between normal and glitched states with hue-rotate(0-180deg), saturate(0.5-2), contrast(0.8-1.5). Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.sequenceDuration || 3, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: glitchKeyframes, easing: 'linear', iterations: params.loop ? 'infinite' : 1}. Input params: Zod schema with glitchFrequency (number), glitchIntensity (number, 0-1), colorShift (number, degrees), sequenceDuration (number), loop (boolean), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: [effectData]}.

prompts.prompt: Develop an internal effect preset called 'prism-refraction' that simulates light passing through a prism, creating beautiful rainbow-like color channel separations. The effect should animate color channels spreading apart like light refracting through glass, with each channel following a slightly different path. Use CSS custom properties to create three duplicate layers (::before, ::after pseudo-elements via JavaScript) each tinted with RGB channels. Animate their positions along bezier curves to create organic, physics-based movement. Parameters should include: refractionAngle (spread angle), prismIntensity (opacity of separated channels), motionCurve (bezier curve definition), and convergencePoint (where channels reunite).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (multiple generic effects). Properties: transform (translateX, translateY following bezier paths), opacity, filter (for channel isolation). Create three effect objects for R, G, B channels with different AnimationRange paths. Red channel: translateX from 0 to -params.refractionAngle, arc motion. Green channel: straight path with slight Y offset. Blue channel: translateX from 0 to +params.refractionAngle, opposite arc. Effect data array: [{type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: 2, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [`${targetId}-red`], ranges: redPath}, {type: 'generic', targetIds: [`${targetId}-green`], ranges: greenPath}, {type: 'generic', targetIds: [`${targetId}-blue`], ranges: bluePath}]. Input params: Zod schema with refractionAngle (number, 0-45 degrees), prismIntensity (number, 0-1), motionCurve (string, cubic-bezier), convergencePoint (number, 0-1 progress), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: effectsArray}.

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'frequency-color-shift' that maps audio frequency bands to different color channels, creating a synaesthetic visualization effect. Low frequencies control red channel displacement, mids control green, and highs control blue. Each channel should move independently based on its frequency band intensity, creating organic color separations that dance with the music. The effect should use CSS variables and calc() functions for real-time updates. Include parameters for: frequencyMapping (which frequencies control which colors), channelSensitivity (array of sensitivities per channel), blurOnPeak (adds motion blur at intensity peaks), and colorBlending (additive vs subtractive).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Waveform (multi-frequency reactive). Three waveform effects for R, G, B channels with different audio properties. Red: {type: 'translate', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: params.channelSensitivity[0] || 0.8}. Green: {type: 'translate', audioProperty: 'mid', sensitivity: params.channelSensitivity[1] || 0.6}. Blue: {type: 'translate', audioProperty: 'treble', sensitivity: params.channelSensitivity[2] || 0.9}. Additional blur effect triggered by peak detection. Effect data: [{type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'parent', mode: 'provider', targetIds: [`${targetId}-red`], props: redWaveform}, {type: 'waveform', targetIds: [`${targetId}-green`], props: greenWaveform}, {type: 'waveform', targetIds: [`${targetId}-blue`], props: blueWaveform}]. Input params: Zod schema with frequencyMapping (object), channelSensitivity (number[3]), blurOnPeak (boolean), colorBlending (enum: 'additive'|'subtractive'), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: effectsArray}.

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'anaglyph-3d-drift' that creates a retro 3D anaglyph effect with drifting color channels. The red and cyan channels should slowly drift apart and together, simulating depth perception changes. The effect should use CSS filters and transforms to create authentic red-cyan 3D glasses effect. Include z-axis rotation for added dimensionality. Parameters should control: depthOffset (channel separation distance), driftPattern (sine, circular, figure-8), driftSpeed (oscillation rate), and vintageFilter (adds grain, vignette, contrast adjustments for retro feel). Perfect for creating nostalgic or retro-futuristic aesthetics.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Properties: filter (for red/cyan channel isolation), transform (translateX, translateZ, rotateY). Create oscillating channel separation using sine wave progression. Red channel: filter: 'sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(-50deg)', translateX animates from 0 to params.depthOffset following sine curve. Cyan channel: filter: 'sepia(1) saturate(2) hue-rotate(130deg)', translateX animates opposite phase. AnimationRange with calculated prog values for smooth oscillation: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 mapping to sine wave positions. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.driftSpeed || 4, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: anaglyphKeyframes, easing: 'ease-in-out', iterations: 'infinite'}. Input params: Zod schema with depthOffset (number, pixels), driftPattern (enum: 'sine'|'circular'|'figure8'), driftSpeed (number, seconds), vintageFilter (boolean), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: [effectData]}.

prompts.prompt: Build an internal effect preset called 'holographic-spectrum' that creates an iridescent, holographic color shifting effect by rapidly cycling through RGB channel offsets in a rainbow pattern. The effect should simulate the appearance of holographic foil or oil slick surfaces. Use CSS custom properties with HSL color space manipulation combined with subtle channel separations. The channels should shift in a wave-like pattern across the element. Include parameters for: spectrumSpeed (color cycle rate), shimmerIntensity (channel offset amount), waveDirection (horizontal, vertical, radial), and metallic (adds metallic sheen via contrast/brightness). Great for futuristic UI elements or attention-grabbing text.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Properties: filter (hue-rotate, brightness, contrast, saturate), transform (for subtle channel offsets), background (gradient overlays). Complex keyframe sequence cycling through full spectrum: hue-rotate from 0deg to 360deg with synchronized channel offsets. AnimationRange: [{key: 'filter', val: 'hue-rotate(0deg) brightness(1)', prog: 0}, {key: 'filter', val: 'hue-rotate(120deg) brightness(1.2)', prog: 0.33}, {key: 'filter', val: 'hue-rotate(240deg) brightness(0.9)', prog: 0.66}, {key: 'filter', val: 'hue-rotate(360deg) brightness(1)', prog: 1}]. Combine with subtle translateX/Y for channel separation at each keyframe. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.spectrumSpeed || 2, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: holographicKeyframes, easing: 'linear', iterations: 'infinite'}. Input params: Zod schema with spectrumSpeed (number), shimmerIntensity (number, 0-1), waveDirection (enum), metallic (boolean), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: [effectData]}.

prompts.prompt: Develop an internal effect preset called 'datamosh-rgb-corruption' that simulates video compression artifacts and datamoshing effects through aggressive RGB channel manipulation. The effect should create the appearance of corrupted video data by randomly displacing and distorting color channels, similar to broken video codecs. Use combinations of skew, scale, and translate transforms per channel with abrupt, glitchy transitions. Include pixel-sorting simulation via CSS clip-path. Parameters: corruptionLevel (intensity of effect), glitchDuration (length of corruption bursts), channelLag (delay between channel updates), and compressionArtifacts (adds blocky, JPEG-like artifacts).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Combined (multiple generic effects with staggered timing). Properties: transform (skewX, skewY, scaleX, scaleY, translateX, translateY), clip-path (for pixel sorting effect), filter (contrast, saturate for compression look). Create three effects with offset start times for channel lag. Red effect: start: 0, abrupt transforms with linear easing. Green effect: start: params.channelLag || 0.1. Blue effect: start: params.channelLag * 2 || 0.2. Each uses different distortion patterns. AnimationRange includes sudden jumps: prog 0, 0.1 (jump), 0.2 (hold), 0.4 (jump), etc. Effect data array: three effect objects with staggered timing and different corruption patterns per channel. Input params: Zod schema with corruptionLevel (number, 0-1), glitchDuration (number), channelLag (number, 0-0.5), compressionArtifacts (boolean), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: effectsArray}.

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'thermal-vision-shift' that simulates thermal camera color channel effects with dynamic heat mapping. The effect should shift between normal colors and thermal-style false color mapping, with RGB channels representing different temperature ranges. Red for hot areas (highlights), blue for cold (shadows), green for mid-tones. Use CSS filters with color matrix manipulation and blend modes. The effect should pulse or transition smoothly between normal and thermal views. Parameters: heatSensitivity (contrast adjustment), thermalIntensity (effect strength), pulseMode (constant vs pulsing), and colorMap (predefined thermal palettes like 'iron', 'rainbow', 'medical').
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Properties: filter (using SVG filter references or CSS filter functions for color matrix), mix-blend-mode. Complex filter string combining: invert(), hue-rotate(), contrast(), brightness() to achieve thermal look. AnimationRange transitioning between normal and thermal: [{key: 'filter', val: 'none', prog: 0}, {key: 'filter', val: 'invert(1) hue-rotate(180deg) contrast(2) brightness(0.8)', prog: 0.5}, {key: 'filter', val: 'none', prog: 1}]. Additional color channel adjustments via RGB filter matrix values. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: 3, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: thermalKeyframes, easing: params.pulseMode === 'pulse' ? 'ease-in-out' : 'linear', iterations: params.pulseMode === 'pulse' ? 'infinite' : 1}. Input params: Zod schema with heatSensitivity (number, 0-2), thermalIntensity (number, 0-1), pulseMode (enum: 'constant'|'pulse'), colorMap (enum: 'iron'|'rainbow'|'medical'), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: [effectData]}.

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'neon-rgb-glow' that creates a cyberpunk-style neon glow effect with separated RGB color channels emanating from the target element. Each color channel should have its own glow radius and intensity, creating layered neon light bleeding. Use multiple text-shadow or box-shadow layers for each RGB component with different blur radii and offsets. The effect should animate the glow intensity and channel separation in a breathing pattern. Parameters: glowRadius (max glow distance), channelIntensity (array for R,G,B intensities), breathingSpeed (pulsation rate), and electricFlicker (adds random flicker for realistic neon). Perfect for cyberpunk titles and UI elements.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: Generic (AnimationRange[]). Properties: textShadow or boxShadow (multiple layers for RGB channels), filter (blur for glow softness). Create complex shadow string with RGB components: '0 0 10px rgba(255,0,0,0.8), 2px 2px 20px rgba(255,0,0,0.6), -2px -2px 30px rgba(0,255,0,0.7), 0 0 25px rgba(0,0,255,0.8)'. AnimationRange for breathing effect: shadow radius and opacity animate from min to max values. Include flicker keyframes if electricFlicker enabled: rapid opacity changes at specific prog points. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.breathingSpeed || 2.5, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: neonGlowKeyframes, easing: 'ease-in-out', iterations: 'infinite'}. Input params: Zod schema with glowRadius (number, pixels), channelIntensity (number[3], 0-1 for RGB), breathingSpeed (number), electricFlicker (boolean), targetIds (string[]). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return: {effects: [effectData]}.
